name: Palazzo Parigi
positioning: Palazzo Parigi Hotel & Grand Spa: an owner-designed luxury hotel in central Milan near La Scala and Brera, with an 18th-century private garden and a large spa
best_for: Travelers who want a central Milan base close to La Scala, Brera and the fashion streets
Guests who want a terrace or balcony and a large spa with a pool and hammam

facts.text: The hotel is at Corso di Porta Nuova 1 in central Milan, close to Teatro alla Scala and a few steps from the major fashion streets.
It sits next to the Brera arts district, and the Brera Art Gallery on Via Brera is not far away.
The hotel was designed by its owner, the Italian architect Paola Giambelli, who also manages it.
The interiors have marble floors and a sweeping staircase, and the lobby has Murano chandeliers and marble pillars.
The rooms were designed by Paola Giambelli together with Paris-based designer Pierre-Yves Rochon.
Rooms come in a Milanese style, more contemporary with cream furnishings and natural wood, or a classically chic Parisian style.
Caffe Parigi, the hotel's cafe and bar, is filled with natural light and draws a local crowd.
Afternoon tea is served in Caffe Parigi or out in the private garden.
The Grand Spa has a large swimming pool, and its hammam can also be booked for private hire.
The spa's fitness area gets plenty of natural daylight.
The spa offers Valmont anti-aging treatments.

highlights.text: A large private garden dating back to the 18th century, with statues and the shade of ancient trees, sits within the hotel.
The Imperial Suite has Duomo views and a private jacuzzi and hammam, and can be joined with two other rooms to form a three-bedroom apartment.
The spa's Royal Hammam Suite is a Moroccan-style space with Moorish architecture and pink marble.
Every bedroom has a terrace or balcony, many with views of the Duomo, the Sforzesco Castle or the Porta Nuova skyline.
In the Gastronomic Restaurant, dishes are delivered through a culinary catwalk.

considerations.text: Views vary by room: many bedrooms look over the city, while some, such as Premium Rooms, may face the courtyard instead.
The two room styles differ, contemporary Milanese or classic Parisian, so it is worth asking for the one you prefer.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive positioning.
